title: The Tarjumán al-Ashwáq
author: ibn-arabi
attributionNote: The attribution is the one the edition and the scholarly consensus give; the catalogue does not adjudicate disputed cases.
description: Sixty-one love poems written in Mecca, published with Ibn Arabi's own commentary, which reads the beloved, the desert and the pilgrimage as figures of the divine. The double reading is the work's argument: the same poem is erotic and metaphysical, and the commentary says which is meant.
historicalContext: Written while Ibn Arabi was in Mecca on pilgrimage. Nicholson's 1911 edition presented the Arabic poems with an English translation and the author's commentary, and remains the standard English access to the work.
availabilityNote: Streamed from Wikisource page by page at read time. The 1911 translation by Reynold A. Nicholson is public domain; the page text is served by Wikisource under its own terms.
